items.q: Internal iliac artery splits into?
items.a: Internal pudendal artery (smaller · pelvic viscera) + caudal gluteal artery (larger)
items.why: Pre-lab video + slide 2: caudal gluteal = LARGER terminal branch

items.q: Branch of the internal iliac to the lateral ligament of the bladder?
items.a: Umbilical artery

items.q: First branch off the caudal gluteal, running dorsally?
items.a: Iliolumbar artery (usually before the cranial gluteal; sometimes straight off the internal iliac)

items.q: Iliolumbar artery ends where (lateral view)?
items.a: Deep surface of the cranial end of the middle gluteal muscle

items.q: Next branch off the caudal gluteal after the iliolumbar?
items.a: Cranial gluteal artery

items.q: Cranial gluteal artery + nerve course?
items.a: Across the cranial part of the greater ischiatic notch, between the middle + deep gluteal muscles, toward the tensor fasciae latae

items.q: Caudal gluteal artery passes which side of the sacrotuberous ligament?
items.a: Lateral to its attachment on the tuber ischii

items.q: Small nerve just MEDIAL to the sacrotuberous ligament at the tuber ischii?
items.a: Caudal cutaneous femoral nerve (may run with a small branch of the caudal gluteal artery)

items.q: Muscles transected for the lateral (gluteal) approach?
items.a: Superficial gluteal, middle gluteal, biceps femoris

items.q: Which limb is dissected?
items.a: The RIGHT pelvic limb

items.q: External iliac arteries arise from?
items.a: Abdominal aorta at the level of lumbar vertebra 6–7, caudal to the caudal mesenteric artery

items.q: External iliac terminates as?
items.a: Femoral artery (bigger) + deep femoral artery (smaller)

items.q: Only branch of the external iliac artery?
items.a: Deep femoral artery — arises inside the abdomen near the vascular lacuna

items.q: Short trunk off the deep femoral artery?
items.a: Pudendoepigastric trunk
items.why: Video spent a long time on it

items.q: Pudendoepigastric trunk splits into?
items.a: External pudendal artery + caudal epigastric artery

items.q: External pudendal artery leaves the abdomen through?
items.a: Inguinal canal → superficial inguinal ring

items.q: Caudal epigastric artery runs on?
items.a: Deep (dorsal) surface of the rectus abdominis, cranially

items.q: If the two arteries come off separately (no trunk)?
items.a: Name them by where they go — caudal epigastric or external pudendal

items.q: Deep femoral after the pudendoepigastric trunk is called?
items.a: Medial circumflex femoral artery
items.why: Video + slide 15: the deep femoral CHANGES NAME

items.q: Medial circumflex femoral course?
items.a: Out through the vascular lacuna, caudally between the quadriceps femoris + pectineus, into the adductor

items.q: Two branches of the medial circumflex femoral?
items.a: Transverse branch + deep branch

items.q: Deep branch of the medial circumflex femoral runs?
items.a: Distally, between the adductor + vastus medialis

items.q: Transverse branch of the medial circumflex femoral runs?
items.a: Transversely/caudally through the adductor → ends in the semimembranosus

items.q: Muscle origins cut to find those branches?
items.a: Gracilis + adductor (pectineus reflected too)

items.q: Entrance to the femoral triangle?
items.a: Vascular lacuna

items.q: Vascular lacuna lies between?
items.a: Caudal border of the external abdominal oblique aponeurosis (inguinal ligament) + the pelvis

items.q: Femoral triangle boundaries?
items.a: Cranial: sartorius · lateral: vastus medialis · caudal: pectineus + adductor

items.q: Contents of the femoral triangle?
items.a: Femoral artery, femoral vein, saphenous nerve

items.q: Femoral artery = continuation of?
items.a: External iliac artery beyond the vascular lacuna

items.q: Small branch from the CRANIAL/lateral side of the femoral, near the top?
items.a: Superficial circumflex iliac artery
items.why: Video: students confused it with the deep circumflex iliac

items.q: Deep circumflex iliac artery comes from?
items.a: Abdominal aorta (deep, inside the abdomen) — runs with the lateral cutaneous femoral nerve

items.q: Larger branch at the same level as the superficial circumflex iliac?
items.a: Lateral circumflex femoral artery

items.q: Lateral circumflex femoral passes between?
items.a: Rectus femoris + vastus medialis

items.q: Three caudal femoral arteries (proximal → distal)?
items.a: Proximal caudal femoral · middle caudal femoral · distal caudal femoral — all off the CAUDAL aspect

items.q: Proximal caudal femoral artery arises?
items.a: Caudal surface of the femoral artery, distal to the lateral circumflex femoral, mid-thigh

items.q: Small artery from the CRANIAL aspect descending to the stifle?
items.a: Descending genicular artery

items.q: Artery from the caudal aspect running with its namesake nerve?
items.a: Saphenous artery (with the saphenous nerve + medial saphenous vein)

items.q: Middle caudal femoral artery dives into?
items.a: Semimembranosus (arises after the femoral passes lateral to it)

items.q: Distal caudal femoral artery arises?
items.a: Caudal surface of the LAST centimeter of the femoral artery (large vessel)

items.q: Muscle transected to expose the distal caudal femoral?
items.a: Medial head of the gastrocnemius

items.q: Saphenous artery arises?
items.a: Femoral artery, proximal to the stifle

items.q: Saphenous artery terminates as?
items.a: Cranial branch + caudal branch

items.q: Cranial branch of the saphenous artery ends as?
items.a: Dorsal common digital arteries (proximal metatarsus)

items.q: Caudal branch of the saphenous artery course?
items.a: Between the medial head of the gastrocnemius + tibia → tarsal tunnel → plantar paw

items.q: Is there a LATERAL saphenous artery?
items.a: No — only a saphenous artery, on the medial side

items.q: Vein with the saphenous artery?
items.a: Medial saphenous vein (artery = plain 'saphenous')

items.q: Medial saphenous vein branches?
items.a: Cranial + caudal branches (tributaries) — travel with the cranial + caudal branches of the saphenous artery

items.q: Lateral saphenous vein travels with an artery?
items.a: No — it does not satellite an artery

items.q: Lateral saphenous vein is formed by?
items.a: Cranial branch + caudal branch

items.q: Most common venipuncture site, DOG pelvic limb?
items.a: Cranial branch of the lateral saphenous vein
items.why: Said twice in the video + slide 44

items.q: Most common venipuncture site, CAT pelvic limb?
items.a: Medial saphenous vein

items.q: Look-alike next to the caudal branch of the lateral saphenous vein?
items.a: Small distally running vein caudal to it — can be sizeable

items.q: Nerve biopsied near the lateral saphenous vein?
items.a: Caudal cutaneous sural nerve (sensory + sympathetic + some motor axons, no obvious deficit)

items.q: Popliteal artery begins where?
items.a: Femoral artery continues as the popliteal after the distal caudal femoral comes off

items.q: Popliteal artery course?
items.a: Between the two heads of the gastrocnemius → over the flexor surface of the stifle → popliteal notch of the tibia (deep to the popliteus muscle)

items.q: Muscle you transect to follow the popliteal artery?
items.a: Popliteus

items.q: Popliteal artery terminates as?
items.a: Cranial tibial artery (large, main continuation) + caudal tibial artery (tiny)

items.q: Which tibial artery won't you find?
items.a: Caudal tibial artery (2–3 tiny branches into the popliteus)

items.q: Cranial tibial artery passes between?
items.a: Tibia + fibula (interosseous space) → lateral crus

items.q: Cranial tibial artery lies between which muscles?
items.a: Cranial tibial muscle + long digital extensor

items.q: Third muscle in that group (lateral)?
items.a: Fibularis (peroneus) longus

items.q: Nerve that runs with the cranial tibial artery distally?
items.a: Deep branch of the common peroneal (fibular) nerve

items.q: Nerve to watch for when reflecting the crural fascia?
items.a: Superficial branch of the common peroneal (fibular) nerve
items.why: Video: he cut some by accident

traps: SAPHENOUS ARTERY is plain 'saphenous' — the vein with it is the MEDIAL saphenous vein. There is NO lateral saphenous artery.
SUPERFICIAL circumflex iliac = branch of the FEMORAL. DEEP circumflex iliac = branch of the AORTA (Lab 23).
Deep femoral artery → gives the pudendoepigastric trunk → then is renamed MEDIAL circumflex femoral. LATERAL circumflex femoral comes off the FEMORAL artery.
Caudal gluteal = LARGER terminal branch of the internal iliac; internal pudendal = smaller.
Venipuncture: DOG = cranial branch of the LATERAL saphenous vein · CAT = MEDIAL saphenous vein. Don't flip them.
Proximal, middle + distal caudal femoral arteries all leave the CAUDAL side; the descending genicular leaves the CRANIAL side.
Popliteal ARTERY runs deep to the popliteUS MUSCLE (the transcript says 'popliteal muscle').
Cranial tibial artery runs between the cranial tibial MUSCLE and the long digital extensor — artery and muscle share a name.
Peroneal = fibular (same nerve; the lab guide says peroneal, the video says fibular).
